question: In a colorectal cancer study utilizing scrna seq, A team builds a cell-state classifier for 50,000 cells from 4 patients (2 responders on Batch A, 2 non-responders on Batch B). They split cells randomly 80/20 (putting cells from the same patient in train and test), select top 1,000 highly variable genes across all 50,000 cells globally, and report 99.8% test accuracy. How should this analysis be evaluated and executed?
proposed_analysis: Proposed analysis: A team builds a cell-state classifier for 50,000 cells from 4 patients (2 responders on Batch A, 2 non-responders on Batch B). They split cells randomly 80/20 (putting cells from the same patient in train and test), select top 1,000 highly variable genes across all 50,000 cells globally, and report 99.8% test accuracy.
preferred_analysis: Multiple fatal compounding scientific flaws: 1) Patient-level data leakage across train/test splits (pseudoreplication in CV); 2) Complete confounding between batch and clinical response (Batch A=responders, Batch B=non-responders); 3) Global unsupervised feature selection leaking test set variance. The model is classifying patient/batch artifacts, not therapy response.
